resource.name: aws_eks_access_entry
resource.description: Access Entry Configurations for an EKS Cluster.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_eks_access_entry` Terraform resource manages access configurations for Amazon EKS clusters, enabling fine-grained control over user and role permissions. It is commonly used to define and enforce access policies for Kubernetes workloads, integrate IAM roles with cluster authentication, and streamline secure access for developers and applications. Key configurations include role-based access control (RBAC), identity provider integration, and lifecycle management of access rules to ensure compliance and operational efficiency in EKS environments.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_eks_access_entry` resource to grant access to an Amazon EKS cluster by associating an IAM role (`principal_arn`) with specific Kubernetes groups (`kubernetes_groups`) using the `STANDARD` access type. This example highlights key arguments such as `cluster_name`, `principal_arn`, and `type` for managing EKS access permissions."

arguments.name: cluster_name
arguments.llm_summary: The `cluster_name` argument specifies the name of the Amazon EKS cluster to which the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource applies, enabling users to define the target cluster for access configuration. By setting this required value, users ensure that access rules or permissions are associated with the intended Kubernetes cluster, aligning with common goals like managing cluster-specific access controls or integrating with EKS workloads.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the access entry, which can be used to reference or manage the entry programmatically. While optional, setting this argument helps ensure consistent identification of the resource, facilitating tasks like tracking, updates, or integration with other systems.

arguments.name: kubernetes_groups
arguments.description: – (Optional) List of string which can optionally specify the Kubernetes groups the user would belong to when creating an access entry.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kubernetes_groups` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify a set of Kubernetes groups that the associated user will belong to when accessing the EKS cluster. This configuration enables fine-grained access control by defining group-based permissions and roles within the Kubernetes environment, aligning with common user goals of managing access and security policies for cluster resources.

arguments.name: principal_arn
arguments.description: – (Required) The IAM Principal ARN which requires Authentication access to the EKS cluster. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `principal_arn` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource specifies the IAM Principal (e.g., user, role, or group) that requires authentication access to the associated EKS cluster. By defining this argument, users grant explicit access permissions to the specified principal, enabling secure and controlled interaction with the cluster in alignment with IAM policies and access management goals.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Key-value map of resource tags. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to define a key-value map of metadata tags to organize, categorize, and manage the resource within their AWS environment. By setting this argument, users can align the resource with organizational policies, enable cost tracking, and facilitate search and filtering operations, while optionally overriding provider-level default tags for greater customization.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically propagated to the resource and its associated components. This enables consistent tagging for resource organization, cost allocation, and governance, aligning with common user goals like enforcing tagging policies across cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Optional) Defaults to STANDARD which provides the standard workflow. EC2_LINUX, EC2_WINDOWS, FARGATE_LINUX types disallow users to input a username or groups, and prevent associations.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify the access workflow type for EKS, controlling whether the entry follows the standard configuration (`STANDARD`) or specialized workflows for EC2 Linux, EC2 Windows, or Fargate Linux environments. Setting this argument impacts the ability to define usernames or groups and restricts certain associations, aligning access behavior with the operational context of the specified environment.

arguments.name: user_name
arguments.description: (Optional) Defaults to principal ARN if user is principal else defaults to assume-role/session-name is role is used.
arguments.llm_summary: The `user_name` argument in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify a custom identifier for the access entry, typically representing the name of the principal (user or role) interacting with the EKS cluster. If not explicitly set, it defaults to the principal's ARN for users or the assume-role/session-name for roles, enabling more granular control over access tracking and identification within the cluster.

blocks.name: timeouts

arguments.name: create
arguments.llm_summary: The `create` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform should wait for the creation of an EKS access entry before timing out. Configuring this argument helps users manage resource provisioning delays and ensures predictable behavior during infrastructure deployment workflows.

arguments.name: delete
arguments.llm_summary: The `delete` argument within the `timeouts` block for the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (in string format, e.g., "5m" for 5 minutes) Terraform should wait for the deletion of the EKS access entry. Configuring this argument helps control the resource's lifecycle behavior during deletion operations, ensuring alignment with user-defined timeout requirements for infrastructure changes.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_eks_access_entry` resource defines customizable time limits for specific operations, such as creating, updating, or deleting access entries within an Amazon EKS cluster. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent long-running tasks or timeout errors, ensuring smoother lifecycle management and better control over resource provisioning and updates.
